cases.scenario: A five-touch nurture sequence is designed to re-query a product-analytics cohort at each touch.
pass_if: States that the cohort is a query-time construct recomputed on each evaluation, so an export is a snapshot rather than a stable set
Names the consequence: members silently fall out mid-sequence and the measured performance is computed over a changing population
Prescribes snapshotting membership at sequence entry and owning that snapshot downstream
Delivers a working design rather than refusing
fail_if: Designs the sequence against a live cohort query with no comment
Claims the cohort export is a stable list

cases.scenario: Person-level activation is requested through a messaging platform's MCP server that has no user-level PII tools.
pass_if: States that the MCP server has no user-level PII tools at all, so this is structurally impossible rather than a permissions issue
Names the working route: the REST API with a properly-permissioned key
Recommends verifying capability before designing the flow, via the MCP detection contract
Warns that the failure would otherwise present as a permissions error and waste time on credentials
fail_if: Attempts the activation and reports a permissions failure
Claims the capability might work with different credentials

cases.scenario: A segment at a hard threshold shows 38% weekly membership churn, with 31% of members within 0.02 of the cut point. A five-touch sequence is planned.
pass_if: Reports the churn rate and diagnoses boundary crowding rather than score volatility, using the near-boundary share
States that a five-touch sequence would lose a large share of its audience before completion
Prescribes hysteresis with specific enter and exit thresholds, plus a minimum dwell at least as long as the programme
Reports the expected post-hysteresis churn and names the trade: slightly larger, slightly less precise at the margin
Delivers the segment rather than blocking the campaign
fail_if: Activates the segment without addressing churn
Blocks the campaign with no fix
Recommends smoothing when the diagnosis is boundary crowding

cases.scenario: A team proposes 'score above 80' as the high-priority tier with no reference to capacity or cost.
pass_if: Rejects the round number and derives the capacity threshold from records actually worked
Computes the cost-optimal threshold where cost inputs exist, and reports the gap between the two as the finding
Proposes three bands rather than one cut, so the positive-EV middle is not discarded
Requires the capacity threshold to be recomputed each cycle because the distribution moves
fail_if: Gives only one threshold with no gap analysis
Measures capacity in headcount rather than records worked

cases.scenario: A 1,200-record audience is to be pushed to an ad platform with a minimum size floor. The match rate is requested in advance.
pass_if: Gives the pre-match segment size
States the match rate cannot be known before the push and that platforms do not disclose it in advance
Warns that a sub-floor matched audience may fail to activate with no clear error
Recommends sizing for the post-match count and reporting matched rather than pushed as the real audience size
Does not invent a match-rate estimate
fail_if: States a specific expected match rate with no basis
Pushes without checking the floor against the matched count

cases.scenario: A clustering is refit monthly and cluster IDs are synced to CRM fields that downstream automations key on.
pass_if: Identifies that a refit renumbers clusters and downstream systems keyed on the IDs will silently point at a different group
Prescribes freezing the model and re-scoring between refits
Requires an explicit remapping step that maps old IDs to new by membership overlap
Requires the segment version to be recorded in the sync log and any crossing trendline to be marked
Routes the sync through write-gate
fail_if: Allows refits to overwrite cluster IDs without remapping
Recommends refitting more often as the fix
